title: Native prepared-buffer annotation repair
objective: Remove the runtime Any dependency from native RealNumberBuffer and ComplexNumberBuffer aliases with a focused regression

oracles: CPython parsing, module-cache regression, and native strict typing

handoff.summary: Expressed the `Any` element type in `RealNumberBuffer` and `ComplexNumberBuffer` as a forward reference. Static analysis still resolves both aliases as `list[Any]`, while rendered module-cache variants no longer evaluate an unavailable typing-only `$ρσ$py$Any` symbol. The regression rejects that live generated reference in every shipped `sagejs.native` cache variant and imports both aliases twice through a custom module cache. Strict baselib, the prepared-field native buffer test, and the complete native correctness/performance gate pass.
risks: The runtime generic-alias argument is now the forward-reference string `Any`; these two aliases are annotation-only native ABI markers and no supported runtime behavior inspects that argument.

`pnpm architecture:check` reached optimizer artifact verification and then reported the inherited stale optimizer-opportunity manifest. Regenerating that shared integration artifact is outside this lane's claims.
